To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Iron Curtain Trail (ICT) and the European Greenbelt (EGB) are both contested tourism products in the German-Czech borderlands, because they commodify contested borderland memories for EU inspired political and economic cross border cooperation.

the Iron Curtain Trail (ICT) and European Green Belt (EGB) tourism projects, which are promoted by the European Commission and the Council of Europe as part of a larger cross border cooperation policy, have been developed in a way that is not viable, does not represent all communities and does not consider equity.
(i) the Iron Curtain Trail is a viable tourism project, (ii) the Sudetenland heritage project is not, and (iii) both projects are contested.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how to deal with the contestation of EU inspired memory projects, and how to ensure the viability of borderland tourism projects as a tool for European cross border cooperation.
how tourism can be used for political and economic purposes and how the resulting commodification of contested borderscopes can be evaluated.

the question of how tourism can be used to promote a European cross border cooperation discourse in the German Czech Iron Curtain Trail and Green Belt borderland, and how it is contested on local levels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the commodification of contested borderscopes for tourism development can only be successful when it is based on a participative and equitable governance across borders.
the Iron Curtain Trail is a more viable and equitable product than the Sudetenland heritage trail.

these tourism projects can be successful in the sense that they have the potential to promote cross border cooperation, but they can also be contested in the sense that this potential is not realized due to the selectivity of the EU inspired memory politics, and the lack of participatory governance across the border.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Iron Curtain Trail is a successful EU tourism project, but it is not successful in its local implementation.
the EU inspired Iron Curtain Trail and European Green Belt are not viable as tourism products and that they are not inclusive of all borderland stakeholders.
the commodification of contested borderland histories is not a viable strategy for cross border cooperation in tourism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EU inspired borderland projects are not viable tourism products unless they are able to overcome the challenges related to the contestations.
EU inspired cross border cooperation is an important tool for the promotion of European integration but it should be more inclusive of the local level.
the EU inspired memory politics in borderlands needs to be more inclusive and participatory in order to be viable and ethical.
